_doc: Inventory of upstream source documents mirrored into the repository, and
therefore redistributed in every checkout and every deployed build.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The corpus licence machinery (NVDM envelopes, the
Headwaters registry, nvdm-encumbrance-report.py, sample-corpus.json) only
ever looked at public/data and public/geojson. public/docs was invisible to
all of it, so a 4.4 MB mirror of CPCB's Polluted River Stretches report
shipped in every checkout while the registry entry for its own source said
the publisher requires approval for any use beyond download and print.
Removing that one file fixes the instance; this manifest plus
scripts/check-mirrored-documents.py fixes the shape, by making every
mirrored document name its source and be gated on that source's terms.
THE RULE. A mirrored document may ship only if its upstream source is
registered in scripts/source-registry/ and does not classify 'restricted'
under scripts/nvdm-encumbrance-report.py. Mirroring is redistribution: a
publisher who requires permission for redistribution has not given it, and
a note in a manifest is not a permission. Extracted factual values are a
different question and are unaffected - facts carry no copyright - which is
why removing a mirror does not mean dropping the numbers derived from it.
WHEN A SOURCE TURNS OUT TO BE RESTRICTED. Delete the mirror and cite the
publisher's own URL. Do not add an exception here. If permission is
actually obtained, record it in `permission` with who granted it, when, and
in what form, and the gate will accept it.
UNRESOLVED entries are permitted but are reported loudly by the checker on
every run. They are a to-do list, not a clearance.

documents.note: KSPCB's own copyright policy page was not retrievable on 2026-07-31 (the Karnataka gov template URL 404s). The Karnataka Open Data Policy 2021 reportedly carries a data-monetisation goal, which is a further unresolved question over every Karnataka state source. Until the policy text is read, this mirror is unproven rather than cleared.

BWSSB's copyright policy page (read 2026-07-31) prints BOTH Karnataka government templates side by side - one permitting republication in any format free of charge with attribution, one requiring prior authorisation - without saying which governs this material. That is not a grant. Separately, BWSSB is a public undertaking and owns its copyright independently under Copyright Act s.17(dd), so the OpenCity CKAN label on the sibling dataset does not reach this PDF. Unproven.
